title: Tuna Noodle Casserole with Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna noodle casserole with mushroom sauce is a hearty dish that combines pasta, canned tuna, mushrooms, and a creamy sauce. Baked until golden, it offers a comforting, protein‑rich meal that has been popular in American home cooking since the mid‑20th century.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in post‑war America as an inexpensive way to use canned tuna.
Mushroom sauce is often made from sautéed mushrooms, flour, and milk, making it lighter than traditional cheese sauces.
Tuna provides a high amount of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.
The casserole stores well in the fridge and can be reheated, making it a common make‑ahead family meal.
Variations may include peas, broccoli, or cheddar cheese for extra flavor and texture.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Tuna supplies EPA and DHA, which support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A serving delivers about 20‑25 g of protein, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna and mushrooms are good sources of niacin, B12, and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from sauce
items.content: The creamy mushroom sauce adds calcium, contributing to bone health.

items.title: Fiber from pasta
items.content: Using whole‑grain pasta boosts dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna is often salty; choose low‑sodium varieties when possible.

items.title: Calorie‑dense sauce
items.content: The creamy sauce adds calories and saturated fat; consider using reduced‑fat milk or cutting back on the amount.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow bacterial growth; keep the casserole refrigerated and consume within 3‑4 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot, often alongside a green salad or steamed vegetables. Sprinkle grated cheese on top a few minutes before the end of baking for a golden crust. Leftovers reheat well in the microwave or oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the casserole to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
